page.text:
A collection of vectors is *linearly independent* if no vector in the set can
be expressed as a linear combination of the remaining vectors. In equational terms,
the only linear combination that yields the zero vector is the trivial one:
$$ c_1 v_1 + c_2 v_2 + \cdots + c_k v_k = 0 \implies c_1 = c_2 = \cdots = c_k = 0. $$
Linear independence ensures that each vector contributes an independent geometric
dimension without redundant information.
